resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and German source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded German pass identified 25 actionable formula, terminology, grammar, and technical-clarity defects across electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, unit, and wire-gauge content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent German human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The current formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘I = V/R’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘I = V / R’.

findings.summary: The resistance formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘R = V/I’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘R = V / I’.

findings.summary: The electrical-power paragraph used the vague loanword Spielraum for a safety margin.
evidence: The previous paragraph said the component needed ‘Spielraum’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise technical phrase Sicherheitsmarge.

findings.summary: The Joule example described a power rate as joules per second without stating the equivalent power.
evidence: The previous conclusion used ‘7,2 Joule pro Sekunde’.
findings.resolution: Clarified the result as 7.2 W or 72 J in 10 seconds.

findings.summary: The heat-transfer bullet retained the English loanword Hardware.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘Hardware’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the German term Geräte.

findings.summary: The parallel-connection definition used a literal compound rather than the standard German term.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘Eine Parallelverbindung ...’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Parallelschaltung.

findings.summary: The series-cell safety bullet used an awkward nominalized phrase for charging.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘Das serielle Lithium-Ionen-Laden’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as charging lithium-ion cells in series and clarified balancing or protection.

findings.summary: The German sentence incorrectly capitalized a new clause after a semicolon.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘; Viele Metalle’.
findings.resolution: Changed Viele to lowercase viele.

findings.summary: The right-triangle explanation used an ungrammatical description of the adjacent side.
evidence: The previous paragraph said the adjacent side ‘berührt ihn mit Ausnahme der Hypotenuse’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the paragraph with standard Gegenkathete, Ankathete, and Hypotenuse wording.

findings.summary: The TCR current formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘I = V/R’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘I = V / R’.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity formula lost the temperature-difference symbol.
evidence: The previous expression was ‘C = Q/AT’.
findings.resolution: Restored ‘C = Q / ΔT’.

findings.summary: The heating-time conclusion used an unclear pronoun and spelled out the protected seconds unit.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended with ‘ist es etwa 523 Sekunden’.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it with the heating time and protected 523 s notation.

findings.summary: The phase-change limitation referred to specific heat rather than specific heat capacity.
evidence: The previous paragraph said ‘die spezifische Wärme’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to die spezifische Wärmekapazität and clarified deviation from the ideal.

findings.summary: The heat-flux description used Wärmefluss instead of the preferred German technical term.
evidence: The previous description repeatedly used ‘Wärmefluss’.
findings.resolution: Aligned the description with Wärmestromdichte.

findings.summary: The heat-flux summary used an indirect literal rate phrase.
evidence: The previous summary described the rate of heat transfer through an area unit indirectly.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Die Wärmeübertragungsrate pro Flächeneinheit’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example title omitted the technical concept of flux density.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Durchschnittlicher Wärmefluss’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Mittlere Wärmestromdichte eines Heizelements’.

findings.summary: The practical heat-flux check used an infinitive rather than a formal imperative.
evidence: The previous bullet began with an infinitive rather than ‘Unterscheiden Sie’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to a formal imperative distinguishing average and local maxima.

findings.summary: The second heat-flux check used an informal or incomplete imperative.
evidence: The previous bullet did not use the formal instruction style used elsewhere in the locale.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Berücksichtigen Sie ...’.

findings.summary: The conduction note used Wärmefluss rather than Wärmestrom.
evidence: The previous bullet said the minus sign indicated ‘Wärmefluss’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the technical term Wärmestrom.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge section title was mistranslated as measuring-device systems.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Messgerätesysteme’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the technical title ‘Drahtstärkesysteme’.

findings.summary: The AWG safety paragraph incorrectly capitalized the second clause after a semicolon.
evidence: The previous paragraph used ‘; Die Strombelastbarkeit’.
findings.resolution: Changed Die to lowercase die and retained the technical safety wording.

findings.summary: The final wire-gauge instruction used the vague phrase aktuelle Kapazität.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘Bestimmen Sie die aktuelle Kapazität’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise term Strombelastbarkeit.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example conclusion used the generic Wärmefluss term after the title was localized.
evidence: The previous conclusion said ‘Die durchschnittliche Wärmefluss ...’.
findings.resolution: Aligned it with mittlere Wärmestromdichte.

findings.summary: The length-conversion formulas retained English unit names and decimal points.
evidence: The previous formulas used inch, foot, feet, and decimal points.
findings.resolution: Localized the unit names and normalized German decimal commas across the formula set.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge comparison used an awkward phrase for stranded construction.
evidence: The previous paragraph used ‘strandete Konstruktion’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the natural German phrase mehrdrähtige Ausführung.
